title: Smithsonian Boss Steps Down After a Year of Fights
summary:
Have you ever been in a fight with someone so big that you just want to walk away? That's kind of what happened to Lonnie Bunch, the guy in charge of the Smithsonian museums in Washington, D.C. He's stepping down at the end of the year after a big clash with President Trump.

Bunch has been the leader of the Smithsonian since 2019. That's the group that runs amazing museums like the National Museum of American History and the Air and Space Museum. But this year, things got really tense. The White House put out a report saying the museum leaders were "radical activists" who can't be trusted. They wanted museums to tell history in a way that is "inspiring, unifying, and worthy of our great republic." That means they wanted a more positive, patriotic story.

Bunch said he's leaving with "very mixed emotions and heartfelt gratitude." That means he's sad but also thankful. Some people think Trump might want to put his own people in charge. But Trump can't just fire Bunch like he did at other places, like the Kennedy Center. The Smithsonian is special—it's not part of the government's main branch. A group called the Board of Regents watches over it, and that includes Vice President JD Vance and Supreme Court Chief Justice John Roberts.

Chief Justice Roberts said Bunch did a great job telling "our nation's story." But the White House didn't say anything when asked about Bunch leaving.

So, what happens next? Nobody knows yet who will take over. But one thing's for sure: telling the story of America is a big job, and it can get really political. Maybe you'll visit the Smithsonian one day and see how they tell it!
why_it_matters: Whoever controls the Smithsonian shapes the stories that millions of kids and families hear about America, so this fight could affect what you see and learn on future museum visits.

background_read: The Smithsonian (a world-famous group of museums in Washington, D.C.) is not run directly by the president; a special group called the Board of Regents watches over it.
The Board of Regents includes Vice President JD Vance (the country's second-highest official) and Chief Justice John Roberts (the top judge of the U.S. Supreme Court).

Lonnie Bunch (the Smithsonian's leader since 2019) is stepping down after President Trump (the U.S. president) and the White House pushed for museums to tell a more patriotic and inspiring American story.

WHERE: Washington, D.C., where the Smithsonian's museums are located.
WHY: The White House wanted a more positive and patriotic story and called museum leaders radical activists, while Bunch said he leaves with mixed emotions and gratitude.
